entries.title: Proverbs 16:1
segments:
CHAP. XVI. 
 
  V. 1. From the Lord-Men can neither think nor speak wisely and well without Divine assistance.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:2
segments: V. 2. Weigheth-Exactly knows as men do the things which they weigh. Spirits-The hearts of men.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:3
segments: V. 3. Commit-Refer all thy actions and concerns to God, as the end of them, and depend upon God's providence for success.  Established-Thy designs shall be brought to an happy issue.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:4
segments: V. 4. Doth work-He orders or disposes.  For-For his own glory; for the discovery of his wisdom, power, goodness, truth, justice. The wicked-Wilful and impenitent sinners.  Men make themselves wicked, and God therefore makes them miserable.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:6
segments: V. 6. By mercy-By a merciful and just and faithful frame of heart and course of life.  Is purged-As they qualify a man to offer up acceptable prayers to God for the pardon of his sins.  By fear-By a filial reverence unto God.  Depart-They are kept from abusing pardoning mercy, and from returning to folly or wickedness.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:9
segments: V. 9. Deviseth-Proposes what he will do.  Directeth-Over-rules and disposes all his designs and actions.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:10
segments: V. 10. A divine sentence-Great sagacity and piercing judgment. Of the king-Of wise kings; who only are worthy of that name and office.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:11
segments: V. 11. The Lord's-Are made by his direction and appointment, so that no man can alter them without violating God's rights and authority.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:15
segments: V. 15. A cloud-As acceptable as those clouds which bring the latter rain, whereby the fruits are filled and ripened a little before the harvest.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:17
segments: V. 17. The high-way-Their common road, in which they walk, tho' through frailty or temptation they slip into the bypath of sin. From evil-From the evil of sin, and consequently from the evil of punishment.  Keepeth-That takes heed to walk in that high-way.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:20
segments: V. 20. Good-He who orders his affairs with discretion.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:21
segments: V. 21. The wise-He who is truly wise, shall be so accounted by others. Sweetness-Eloquence added to wisdom.  Increaseth-Both in himself, for while a man teaches others, he improves himself; and others, who by this means are induced to hear and receive his instructions.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:22
segments: V. 22. The instruction-Their most grave and serious counsels are foolish.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:23
segments: V. 23. Teacheth-Directs him what to speak, and keeps him from speaking foolishly.  Addeth-Enables him to speak learnedly and wisely.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:27
segments: V. 27. Diggeth up-Prosecutes his evil designs with great industry. His lips-His tongue is set on fire of hell.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:30
segments: V. 30. Shutteth-That his thoughts may be more intent. Moving-Which is the gesture of one whose thoughts are deeply engaged.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:32
segments: V. 32. Is better-Of a more gallant and generous spirit, and more valiant and victorious.

entries.title: Proverbs 16:33
segments: V. 33. The lot-As the ancient practice was in deciding doubtful things. The event of which though casual to men, is directed by God's providence.
